generalfeedback.text:
A point is in \(R\) if it makes all three inequalities true. Points on a solid edge are included; points on a dashed edge are not.

(a) For example \(({@tp[1][1]@}, {@tp[1][2]@})\) or \(({@tp[2][1]@}, {@tp[2][2]@})\).

(b) Counting row by row, the whole-number points in \(R\) are \({@pts@}\): there are \({@n@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: whole-number points in a required region

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Give a point with whole-number coordinates in a region defined by three inequalities, and count all such points.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 1 (Graphing inequalities), Section D, question D4(b) of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new systems with solid and dashed edges, the unwanted sides shaded, and a give-a-point part.
